content:
Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness tracker similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. Having used WHOOP for the past six months, I do think the concept is great, but there are several aspects I hope Apple can do better.

We don't have many details about the appearance of Apple's screenless fitness tracker yet, as the product is still in a fairly early stage of development. It's not expected to launch until at the earliest 2028. Bloomberg described it as 'a slim fabric band with a built-in sensor computing module'.

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase on a promotion where Sapphire cardholders could get a WHOOP at a discount or for free—I took advantage of it then. Since then, I've been using WHOOP—though I've never really fully committed to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection can never be perfect, and I find that whether before or after a workout, you have to take out your phone to log the activity, which is annoying. With Apple Watch, you can start a workout directly on the watch face, while WHOOP syncs the time through Apple Health. That's the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If it's a gym workout, taking out your phone is fine, but if it's a casual bike ride or a walk, I don't want to have to bother pulling out my phone.

So, for Apple's screenless fitness tracker, I hope to see some kind of button plus indicator light design that can be used to start and stop workout tracking. You'd still need to categorise the workout on your phone afterwards, but I'd rather do it later than deal with it in the moment. Apple could also develop a classification model based on several factors.

Summary

If Apple can successfully develop a screenless fitness tracker that doesn't feel cumbersome to use even without a phone, I think it would be very appealing. This form factor has many advantages, including comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to wear a traditional watch at the same time.

Top comment posted by TB

I bought a FitBit Air because after years of almost exclusively wearing an Apple Watch, I've started to find it tiring. I love mechanical watches, but at the same time I want to continue tracking my health and enjoy the conveniences of a smartwatch, such as using Apple Pay without taking out my phone, unlocking doors with my watch when my hands are full, and so on. If Apple releases a similar product that can deeply integrate into its ecosystem, let me use a lite version of Apple Pay, home keys, car keys, and other NFC features, while also connecting to AirPods to have notifications read to me via Siri or have actions performed for me, I'll be first in line to buy it.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I found that I still prefer a smartwatch, even at the cost of worse battery life. I understand some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on Do Not Disturb on my watch is enough.

What do you think about Apple developing a screenless fitness tracker? What price would make you willing to buy one? Let us know in the comments.
